Maia for Support response drafts

Draft a support response grounded in the case and approved guidance.

Help agents respond with the right context while preserving their judgment. Maia prepares a sourced draft, and the case owner checks facts, recipients, and promises.

All use cases ↗

Start with the whole relevant case

Give Maia the authorized ticket history, current product details, and the procedures that apply. Include earlier promises and troubleshooting so the draft does not ask the customer to repeat completed work.

State who will receive the message and which support channel it belongs to. A public reply, a private account contact, and an internal note need different detail.

Ground each step in guidance

Ask Maia to link proposed instructions to the current support document or approved case record. If two procedures conflict, it should stop and present the conflict. If the answer depends on a product state that the record does not show, the draft should ask for that information.

This approach is especially useful for edge cases. The agent can inspect why Maia suggested a step instead of trusting a polished but unsupported answer.

Write for the customer in front of you

A good response acknowledges the specific problem, says what is known, gives the next useful step, and sets an accurate expectation. It should not paste a long procedure when the customer needs one action.

Maia can adapt approved guidance to the case, but it should not promise refunds, deadlines, fixes, or account changes that the source and agent do not authorize. Mark uncertainty plainly.

Keep the agent in control

Post the draft in the support Slack thread. The assigned agent verifies identity, case state, technical accuracy, tone, recipients, and allowed commitments. A specialist can correct an instruction before the message leaves the team.

This workflow ends with a reviewed draft. Sending and any account action stay with authorized support staff and systems.

Begin with a common question

Choose a resolved ticket type with current guidance. Ask Maia to draft a response, then compare it with the approved resolution. Look for stale links, missed context, or wording that overstates certainty. Improve the source guidance when the same ambiguity appears repeatedly.

Questions from support teams

Can Maia answer without a support article?

It can summarize the case and draft clarifying questions. For product instructions or policy, provide a current approved source.

What if the customer asks for an exception?

The draft can identify the request and the policy involved. An authorized agent or manager decides whether an exception is allowed.

Does Maia send replies automatically?

This example prepares a draft in Slack. The assigned agent reviews and sends it through the approved support channel.
